The '''2010–11 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 109th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 79th in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the 1st since its organization under [[Lega Serie A|a league committee]] separate from [[Serie B]]. It began on 28 August 2010 and ended on 22 May 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Serie A – Results and fixtures|url=https://int.soccerway.com/national/italy/serie-a/2010-2011/regular-season/matches/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240109084549/https://int.soccerway.com/national/italy/serie-a/2010-2011/regular-season/r12352/matches/|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 January 2024|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=27 April 2011}}</ref> [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] were the [[2009–10 Serie A|defending champions]].

[[AC Milan]] won the 2010–11 Serie A and their 18th league title overall with a scoreless draw away to [[AS Roma|Roma]] on 7 May 2011.<ref name="Soccernet.com">{{cite news|title=Milan seal Scudetto glory|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/916407/milan-seal-scudetto-glory-with-draw?cc=5739|access-date=8 May 2011|newspaper=ESPN Soccernet|date=7 May 2011|archive-date=24 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024211730/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/916407/milan-seal-scudetto-glory-with-draw?cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref> This result ensured that with two rounds remaining AC Milan's nearest rival Internazionale could only draw level on points, and AC Milan holds the tiebreaker based on their better head-to-head record.<ref>{{cite news|title=Milan win Italian title to end Internazionale's dominance|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/may/08/milan-serie-a-title|access-date=9 May 2011|newspaper=The Guardian|date=7 May 2011}}</ref> The result prompted celebrations at AC Milan's [[Piazza del Duomo, Milan|Piazza del Duomo]].<ref>{{cite news |title=European round-up: Milan crowned Serie A champions |url=http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/news/European-round-up-AC-Milan-win-18th-Serie-A-championship-article733662.html |newspaper=Mirror Football |date=8 May 2011|access-date=12 May 2013}}</ref> The trophy was presented at AC Milan's next home game on 14 May.<ref>{{cite news |title=Serie A – Milan draw to win title |url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/08052011/58/serie-milan-draw-win-title.html |newspaper=Eurosport.com |date=7 May 2011|access-date=12 May 2013}}</ref>

It was AC Milan's first [[Scudetto]] since 2004 and it ended a run of five successive Serie A titles by their rival Internazionale. It was the first league title for manager [[Massimiliano Allegri]], winning in his first year with AC Milan and who was for many a surprise choice as manager.<ref>{{cite news|title=Allegri proves he's up to title task|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/Allegri-proves-hes-up-to-title-task/articleshow/8193147.cms|access-date=8 May 2011|newspaper=The Times of India|date=8 May 2011}}</ref> AC Milan led the table for most of the season<ref name="Soccernet.com" /> and secured the title with two games remaining. Notably, they defeated defending champions Internazionale twice during the season and also did the same to third place challenger [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]].<ref name="How Milan won">{{cite news|title=How Milan won the Serie A title|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1717/editorial/2011/05/07/2459024/how-ac-milan-won-the-serie-a-title|access-date=9 May 2011|newspaper=Goal.com|date=9 May 2011}}</ref> AC Milan were credited for strengthening their squad with [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] and [[Robinho]] in the summer as well as picking up [[Antonio Cassano]] and [[Mark van Bommel]] in January.<ref name="How Milan won" />
<!--In addition, a new match ball – the [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] [[Nike Total 90 Tracer|T90 Tracer]] – will serve as the official ball for all matches.{{cn}}-->

This would be the last Scudetto not won by Juventus until the [[2020–21 Serie A]].

==Rule changes==
The rules for the registration of non-EU (or non-[[EFTA]] or Swiss) nationals transferred from abroad were revised in the summer of 2010 and announced on 2 July 2010. Clubs could only sign one (rather than two previously) non-EU player and that player could only be signed if a current member of the squad who was not an EU national had been sold or sold abroad.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/35.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_25259_StrilloAreaStampa_upfDownload.pdf|title=CONSIGLIO FEDERALE|date=2 July 2010|access-date=3 July 2010|work=FIGC|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120813150334/http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/35.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_25259_StrilloAreaStampa_upfDownload.pdf|archive-date=13 August 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/25260/2010/07/News.shtml|title=Su extracomunitari, vivai, Club Italia e Settori le prime misure della FIGC|date=2 July 2010|access-date=3 July 2010|work=FIGC|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100706165848/http://www.figc.it/it/204/25260/2010/07/News.shtml|archive-date=6 July 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> The late announcement of this rule change meant that some clubs had to cancel incoming transfers. [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]], for example, were to sign both Colombian [[Pablo Armero]] from Brazilian side [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]], who subsequently signed for [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] instead, and Brazilian agency player [[Zé Eduardo (footballer, born 1991)|Zé Eduardo]], but had to choose between them and eventually transferred the latter. Their outgoing transfer was [[Julio César de León]], who moved to Chinese team [[Shandong Luneng Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng Taishan]].
{{Clear}}

==Teams==
The league featured 17 teams returning from the [[2009–10 Serie A]], plus three teams promoted from [[2009–10 Serie B]] (two as direct promotions, one as playoff winners). On 30 May 2010, [[US Lecce|Lecce]] and [[AC Cesena|Cesena]] won direct promotion to the Serie A by finishing first and second, respectively. [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] became the third Serie B team promoted on 13 June 2010 by winning the promotion playoff final 2–1 on aggregate over [[Torino FC|Torino]]. It was a quick turn-around for Lecce, which spent only one year in Serie B after being relegated from the [[2008–09 Serie A]]. Cesena last played in Serie A in [[1990–91 Serie A|1990–91]], while Brescia played five seasons in Serie B after being relegated from A in [[2004–05 Serie A|2004–05]].
